messages:
diego: Heads-up — p95 latency spiked in eu-berlin POP starting ~2026-11-14T02:10Z. p95 up from 110ms → 480ms, p99 > 1s. Throughput down ~30%.

emily: I see it in SLO dashboard — request rate flat, CPU on hosts OK, but retransmits jumped. tcp retransmits +3x on pop-ber1

zach: ran traceroute from pop-ber1 to upstream peer, looks like PMTU/ICMP filtered on hop 5. Path MTU might be dropping causing fragmentation/retries.

diego: any recent runtime changes to kernel selection or batching? We pushed kernel selector tweak in canary earlier.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: eng-runtime/kernel-selector v1.11 -> canary @ 2026-11-14T01:55Z

claire: runtime traces show kernel-selection oscillating between kernel-A (fast) and kernel-B (safe) at ~600ms intervals. KV cache miss rate up 2.1x during oscillation.

claire: profiler dump snippet:
```
[13:10:23] kernel_choice: A -> B (latency_drop)
[13:10:24] batch_size: 64 -> 16
[13:10:25] kv_cache_evictions: 120/s -> 420/s
```

emily: tcpdump from host: shows PMTU blackhole signature — large packets dropped, then fallback to smaller MSS => bursts of reordering
```
13:09:58.123 IP 10.0.4.2 > 93.184.216.34: Flags [P.], seq 1:1451, ack 1, win 64240, length 1450
13:09:58.124 IP 10.0.4.2 > 93.184.216.34: frag reassembled? N/A
```

raj: This fits: batching heuristic expands batch based on RTT distribution; when path degrades we suddenly get bigger BDP, but kernel selector sees tail shifts and flips to conservative kernel, which reduces throughput and causes evictions.

diego: Suggested mitigation: 1) temporarily cap max_batch_tokens to 32 on berlin pop 2) pin kernel selector to kernel-B safe variant for all requests in pop for next 30m 3) revert canary if runway

zach: I can add PMTU fallback rule on the border firewall and force ICMP allow for that path. Doing now.

raj: I'll push runtime config: cap_batch=32, kernel_force=safe for pop-ber1. Patching in 2m.

deploy-bot: config-change: runtime/config pop-ber1 cap_batch=32,kernel_force=kernel-B @ 2026-11-14T02:18Z

emily: after cap, p95 dropped back to ~130ms within 3 mins. retransmits back to baseline. Throughput recovering. :thumbsup:

diego: nice. Can we still do postmortem? Owners: diego, emily, zach, claire, raj. Action items: add PMTU detection alert, introduce hysteresis to kernel selector, change batching heuristic to not overshoot on sudden RTT spikes.

claire: will capture more traces and produce perf/regression PR for kernel selector hysteresis.

zach: I'll follow up with carrier ops to confirm who is filtering ICMP on that path.

infra-bot: incident created: INF-2026-berlin-mtu-batching-1 assigned to diego

diego: thanks — marking as resolved for now. Will run canary rollback to v1.10 after we have mitigation and better selector.
